lead.why: The abstract names no compound. Main follow-up experiment: 'we selected compounds 16, 22, and 92 for in vivo pharmacokinetic (PK) analysis'; of these only 22 was taken further ('We selected compound 22 for oral bioavailability', 52% at 20 mg/kg; plasma protein binding also by ultrafiltration for 22). Rule 2 applied, 22 chosen as the one taken furthest.

reactions.conditions: General Procedure A: amine (1.0 equiv), sulfonyl chloride (1.1 equiv), iPr2NEt (1.5 equiv), CH2Cl2, rt, overnight; 69%, light orange solid, mp 132-135 C.
reactions.source: Main article, Experimental Section (entry for compound 22: 'Reaction of amine 1a with 4-(difluoromethoxy)benzene-1-sulfonyl chloride (Procedure A)'); Scheme 1; no SI file

notes: Lead choice is a judgement call: three compounds (16, 22, 92) went into PK, and 22 alone into oral bioavailability. 16 (4-Cl analogue) is also a one-step sulfonylation of 1a but is not the lead under the rule as applied. Amine 1a and the sulfonyl chloride are not stated as 'purchased' in so many words; the text says 'commercially available aryl- or heteroaryl-sulfonyl chlorides' and treats the bipiperidines 1a-c as starting materials with no preparation anywhere in the paper, so both are taken as commercial. Product structure derived from the printed name (the text layer has no drawn structures).
